stories.headline: Nvidia shares tumble as company probes CEO Jensen Huang's ties to alleged Chinese intelligence operative
stories.summary: Nvidia fell roughly 4-5% over two sessions after Huang admitted in a memo to an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials suspect may have links to Chinese intelligence; reports allege about $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips may have been diverted to Chinese firms since 2023. Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation, and analysts flagged elevated 'key-person risk' given how closely tied the company's AI strategy is to Huang. The selloff was largely isolated to Nvidia, while rival chipmakers rallied on the news.

stories.headline: Hotter-than-expected October CPI sends Treasury yields surging, lifts odds of a December Fed rate hike
stories.summary: October core CPI rose 0.3% month-over-month versus the 0.2% expected, pushing the 2-year Treasury yield up 17 basis points (its biggest one-day jump since April 2025) and the 10-year yield up 10 basis points to 4.98%, briefly touching 5%. Fed Governor Chris Waller said he would consider backing a 50-basis-point 'jumbo' hike in December if core inflation keeps printing at 0.3% or higher, and traders now price a 91% chance of a quarter-point hike (9% odds of a half-point move), up from 77% a week earlier. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all slipped on the report, with the Nasdaq down about 0.7-0.75%.

stories.headline: Chip stocks ex-Nvidia rally hard as sector rebounds from its steepest one-day drop in 19 months
stories.summary: AMD surged about 13%, Broadcom rose 8%, Intel climbed 5%, and Taiwan Semiconductor gained nearly 4%, while equipment maker ASML added 6% and memory makers Micron and SK Hynix each rose over 5%. The rally came as traders rotated out of Nvidia-specific concerns and bought the broader semiconductor complex, which had been hit by a 21% one-month decline in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tied to post-election uncertainty over AI datacenter buildout timelines.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs calls semiconductor stocks 'oversold,' names Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD as top buys
stories.summary: Goldman analyst James Schneider said chip stocks are 'now clearly in oversold territory' after the Philly Semiconductor Index fell 21% over the past month and the S&P 500 lost 4.3% (about $3 trillion in value) on November 5 amid worries over AI datacenter buildout timelines. Schneider argued Nvidia and Broadcom look attractive even under conservative growth assumptions, trading at roughly 12x and 13x respectively, while AMD is a buy despite less favorable valuation metrics.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $70-$78/share for ~$1.4 trillion valuation, discloses key AI safety threshold has been triggered
stories.summary: Anthropic began its IPO roadshow after setting a price range of $70-$78 per share, valuing the company around $1.4 trillion including all potential shares; trading could begin as soon as November 19. The offering is accompanied by a $26 billion private placement, with Nvidia and Google each committing $10 billion. Separately, Anthropic disclosed that a safety threshold in its Responsible Scaling Policy has been crossed because AI is now accelerating its own R&D enough to roughly double the pace of model improvement, triggering additional internal safeguards rather than halting operations.

stories.headline: OpenAI's CFO calls Q3 a 'blockbuster quarter' as revenue jumps 50% to $10 billion
stories.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said Q3 revenue hit $10 billion, up 50% quarter-over-quarter (versus 18% growth in Q2), putting the company on an annualized run rate near $50 billion. Enterprise revenue doubled sequentially on products like Coding, Cyber and the Dots agent platform, consumer sales grew 20%, subscribers topped 100 million, and weekly active users reached 1.2 billion; OpenAI still trails rival Anthropic in total revenue, underscoring intensifying competition in AI.

stories.headline: Alphabet gains on new AI chip systems announcement, seen as alternative to Nvidia
stories.summary: Alphabet shares rose more than 1% after the company unveiled new AI chip systems, which analysts flagged as a sign of emerging competitive alternatives in the semiconductor/AI-accelerator market just as Nvidia faces company-specific turmoil over its CEO.

stories.headline: Zacks highlights beaten-down value picks after AI stock plunge: Micron, SanDisk, Sanmina, Sterling, Comfort Systems
stories.summary: Zacks' Value Investor column notes that AI-linked stocks have plunged despite strong earnings and rising forecasts, and flags five names trading at attractive valuations after the pullback: Micron (MU), SanDisk (SNDK), Sanmina (SANM), Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) and Comfort Systems USA (FIX).
